query: What army did the namesake of the ship launched as the München in 1930 fight in during the American Revolutionary War?

pipeline_result.response: The name "SS General von Steuben" refers to the ship's maiden voyage as the "General von Steuben", which was launched on 6 September 1757. The ship sailed from Germany to America, where it served as a passenger liner and later an armed transport during the American Revolutionary War.
retrieved_context: SS General von Steuben: SS "General von Steuben was a German passenger liner and later an armed transport in the Kriegsmarine of Nazi Germany that was sunk during World War II.  She was launched as München (sometimes spelled Muenchen), renamed in 1930 as General von Steuben (after the famous German officer of the American Revolutionary War), and renamed again in 1938 as Steuben".

Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette: Marie-Joseph Paul Yves Roch Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette (] ; 6 September 1757 – 20 May 1834), in the United States often known simply as Lafayette, was a French aristocrat and military officer who fought in the American Revolutionary War.  A close friend of George Washington, Alexander Hamilton, and Thomas Jefferson, Lafayette was a key figure in the French Revolution of 1789 and the July Revolution of 1830.

Germans in the American Revolution: Ethnic Germans served on both sides of the American Revolutionary War.  Many supported the Loyalist cause and served as allies of Great Britain, whose King George III was also the Elector of Hanover.  Other Germans came to assist the rebelling American patriots, but most of the Germans who were patriots were colonists.
